activity.role: Commander of I Armored Corps (second appointment)
activity.notes: Distinct 1943 return to I Armored Corps after relinquishing II Corps and before redesignation as US Seventh Army for Sicily. Same institution as 1942 first command; separate noncontinuous activity, do not create a second I Armored Corps sovereign Polity.

sources.title: Library of Congress — George S. Patton (1885–1945): Timeline
sources.citation_text: Library of Congress chronology: 1916 Pershing's Punitive Expedition; 1918–1921 304th Tank Brigade; 1938–1940 Third Cavalry; 1940–1941 Second Armored Brigade; 1941–1942 Second Armored Division; 1942 I Armored Corps; 1942–1943 Western Task Force/II Corps; 1943 resuming I Armored Corps; 1943–1944 Seventh Army; 1944–1945 Third Army; 1945 Fifteenth Army.

spatial_disposition.evidence: Person-specific US military unit/office is not a sovereign Polity. Reuse existing US historical Polity on exact live Production preflight after 402 quota pause, no invented unit-as-Polity, German occupation state or personal place-function UUID. Distinguish father George Smith Patton (1856–1927), Patton IV, and fictional alternate-history derivative.
